kb_proposals: Rigidity of a flat E0-morphism on the universal cover: GX.E0AxisNoLimit.exists_eqOn_smul_dev gives kappa o psi o cov = g • btzPaperDev on any preconnected set of {r > 0} mapped into W ∩ psi^-1(dom kappa), cov (tau, r, theta) = (tau, r e^{i theta}); no slit sector, no angle bookkeeping. Use it instead of exists_eqOn_sectorSmulInl whenever a curve or a region winds around the axis.

A curve off the axis lifts to the universal cover inside one component (open-closed argument with GX.E0AxisNoLimit.sect, the local section of cov, and the deck translations theta -> theta + 2 pi k); see the hlift step of flat_curve_noLimit.

A blunt spear chart into a flat N has no limit along ANY continuous curve of bspear v R with rad -> 0 (GX.E0AxisNoLimit.flat_axis_noLimit); no height bound is needed, and the in-falling ray at a = v (on the vertex's null cone) is included (flat_infall_noLimit_of_le).
notes: One new scaffold module, 0 sorry, standard axioms; lake build GXScaffold.BTZ.AxisNoLimit built only this module. Statement stronger than the roadmap's: the height bounds [a1, a2] and v < a1 are not needed (only v <= fcoord, i.e. the curve stays in the blunt spear), and rad <= R is not needed along the curve. The roadmap's [r] route was followed with two changes: (1) rigidity is done once on the universal cover (exists_eqOn_smul_dev) rather than per slit sector; (2) the developed time tau + r theta^2/2 converges but tau itself need not (a winding curve can converge in E0 to a different axis point than its development), so the holonomy contradiction is run not on a neighbourhood {|tau - a| < eps} of an axis point but on an arc theta -> (T + r pi^2/2 - r theta^2/2, r, theta) at constant developed time T, reached from one late lift by a vertical segment. The fallback form (gamma converges in E0 to an axis point) was not needed. For graduation: the strict GX.E0BluntSpear.flat_infall_noLimit_of_pos becomes a corollary (flat_infall_noLimit_of_le, with v <= a).
